Starting from counting routes by hand, you learn to break a big problem into a table and fill it in cell by cell; in the end you wire up the circuit boards that count routes, compare words and pack a backpack, and see why they are so fast.

只留一行原地改写。改写的方向，决定每件物品能用几次。: Keep just one row and rewrite it in place. The direction you rewrite in decides how many times each item can be used.

前面某个位置能切开，而且那一截刚好是个词，这里就能切开。: If some earlier position can be split and the piece from there to here is exactly a word, this position can be split too.

这张图不能有圈：A 等着 B，B 又等着 A，谁也算不出来。箭头有方向、又绕不成: The graph must have no loops: if A waits for B while B waits for A, neither can ever be worked out. A graph whose arrows have a direction and never loop round is called a directed acyclic graph (DAG).

这些小问题叫<b>子问题</b>。「到学校有几条路线」可以拆成「到学校的上一站各: The small problems are called subproblems. “How many routes lead to school?” breaks down into “how many routes lead to each stop just before school?”, and those break down again, all the way back to the start.

一格的答案怎么从别的格子算出来，这条规则叫<b>状态转移</b>；写成式子，就是: The rule for working out a cell from other cells is called the transition; written as a formula it is a recurrence, such as “this crossing = up + left”.
找规则的老办法是<b>只看最后一步</b>：到这里之前，最后一步可能从哪里来？每: The trusty way to find the rule is to look only at the last step: just before arriving here, where could the last step have come from? Each possibility matches a cell that has already been worked out, and you combine them.
在游戏里，电路板就是状态转移：只写一次，机器人在每一格上都照着它算。: In the game, the circuit board is the transition: written once, and followed by the robot on every cell.
规则总要从某处开始。像起点这样不用再拆的小问题，答案是直接定下的，叫<b>边界条: A rule has to start somewhere. Small problems that need no further breaking down, like the start, have answers that are simply given; these are the base cases. Standing at the start, for instance, counts as 1 route.
表的边上，有的来路落在表外，那里没有路，用「—」表示。规则要能对付这些「—」，边: Along the edges of the table, some ways in fall outside it; there is no road there, and that shows as “—”. The rule has to cope with these “—”s, or the edge cells come out wrong.

同一副骨架能回答不同的问题。问<b>有几种</b>，就把所有来路加起来；问<b>: The same skeleton answers different questions. To ask how many, add up all the ways in; to ask what is best, pick the best of the ways in, then count in this cell’s own cost.
在电路板上，这往往只差一个汇合器的操作：「加起来」数个数，「取较小」找最少，「取: On the circuit board, the difference is often just the Merger’s operation: “sum” counts, “min” finds the fewest, “max” finds the most.

表告诉你最好的结果是多少，却没直接说该怎么走。不过每一格的数，都是从某一条来路算: The table tells you what the best result is, but not straight out how to get it. Yet every cell’s number came from one of its ways in: the table has also kept every choice.
从终点出发，问「这一格的数是从哪条来路来的」，退到那一格，再问同样的问题，一直退: Start at the end and ask “which way in did this cell’s number come from?”, step back to that cell, and ask again, all the way back to the start: you have recovered the whole route. Working backwards like this is called backtracking.
直接「问路」：想知道第 n 级台阶有几种走法，就去问第 n − 1 级和第 n: Ask your way down: to know how many ways lead to step n, ask step n − 1 and step n − 2, which ask further down in turn… and the same small question gets asked again and again. These are overlapping subproblems.

问路法里，台阶每多一级，提问次数就要乘上一个固定的倍数。这种越滚越大的增长叫<b: With the asking method, every extra step multiplies the number of questions by a fixed factor. Growth that snowballs like this is exponential: add a few more steps and the asking never finishes.

动态规划快，不是因为哪一步算得巧，而是因为<b>不重复</b>：指数多的路线，被: Dynamic programming is fast not because any one step is clever, but because nothing is repeated: an exponential number of routes is squeezed into a polynomial number of cells.
表里一格代表的那种情况，叫一个<b>状态</b>，比如「站在这个路口」或「看完了: The situation a cell of the table stands for is called a state, such as “standing at this crossing” or “having seen the first few houses”. The number in the cell is that state’s answer.
好的状态，要记住<b>所有会影响未来的信息</b>。如果两段不同的经历落进了同一: A good state remembers everything that affects the future. If two different histories land in the same cell but can go on to do different things, that cell cannot keep an accurate answer.
设计状态，是动态规划里最难、也最要紧的一步：先想清楚每一格记着什么，规则才写得出: Designing the state is the hardest and most important step in dynamic programming: only once you know what each cell holds can you write its rule.
